tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text:
Income taxes represent a composite of the income taxes attributable to our wholly owned operations and income taxes attributable to our joint ventures with Carrier Global Corporation (“Carrier”), which are primarily taxed as partnerships for income tax purposes; therefore, Carrier is responsible for its proportionate share of income taxes attributable to its share of earnings from these joint ventures. lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Short-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for the cash they will return: financial.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: Sales of HVAC equipment, which we currently source from approximately 20 vendors, accounted for 67% and 69% of our revenues in 2025 and 2024, respectively.
Sales of other HVAC products, which we currently source from more than 1,300 vendors, comprised 29% and 27% of our revenues in 2025 and 2024, respectively.
Sales of commercial refrigeration products, which we currently source from approximately 150 vendors, accounted for 4% of our revenues in both 2025 and 2024.
Combined, our joint ventures with Carrier represented 53% of our revenues in 2025.

We distribute products manufactured by Flexible Technologies, Inc., a subsidiary of Smiths Group plc (“Flexible Technologies”), Resideo Technologies, Inc. (“Resideo”), Southwark Metal Mfg. Co. (“Southwark”), Johns Manville, a subsidiary of Berkshire Hathaway, Inc. (“Johns Manville”), and Owens Corning Insulating Systems, LLC (“Owens Corning”), among others.
We distribute products manufactured by Copeland Corporation, LLC (“Copeland”), The Chemours Company (“Chemours”), Mueller Industries, Inc. (“Mueller”), and Pentair, Inc. (“Pentair”), among others.
The Company’s top ten suppliers accounted for 85% of our purchases, including 62% from Carrier and 8% from Rheem.
The Company’s top ten suppliers accounted for 85% of our purchases during 2025, including 62% from Carrier and 8% from Rheem.

Products supplied by Carrier include a diverse variety of brands of HVAC equipment including Carrier, Bryant, Payne, Tempstar, Heil, Comfortmaker, and Grandaire (a private label product created by the Company), along with complimentary replacement parts.

Given the significant concentration of our supply chain, particularly with Carrier and Rheem, any significant interruption by any of the key manufacturers or suppliers or a termination of a relationship could temporarily disrupt the operations of certain of our subsidiaries.
Our success has also depended on the contributions and abilities of our store employees upon whom we rely on to give customers a superior in-store experience.
Accordingly, our performance depends on our ability to recruit and retain high quality employees to work in and manage our stores.
The amount of future dividends that we will pay, if any, will depend upon a number of factors.

Future dividends will be declared and paid at the sole discretion of the Board of Directors and will depend upon such factors as cash flow generated by operations, profitability, financial condition, cash requirements, potential dilution related to our dividend reinvestment plan, prospects, and other factors deemed relevant by our Board of Directors.

s.t: The condensed consolidated unaudited financial statements include (i) the accounts of Watsco and its wholly owned subsidiaries, (ii) the accounts of five U.S. joint ventures and their subsidiaries with Carrier Global Corporation , which we refer to as Carrier, in which we have an 80 % controlling interest and Carrier has a 20 % non-controlling interest, (iii) the accounts of a Canadian joint venture with Carrier, in which we have a 60 % controlling interest and Carrier has a 40 % non-controlling interest, and (iv) a 38.4 % investment in Russell Sigler, Inc. (“RSI”), owned by one of the joint ventures referred to in (ii) above that is accounted for under the equity method of accounting.

s.t: Carrier Enterprise I also has a 38.4% ownership interest in Russell Sigler, Inc. (“RSI”), an HVAC distributor operating from 36 locations in the Western U.S. RSI is Carrier’s second largest independent North American distributor and had sales of approximately $1.2 billion in 2025.

In 2011, we formed a second joint venture with Carrier, which we refer to as Carrier Enterprise II, in which Carrier contributed company-owned locations in the Northeast U.S., and we contributed certain locations operating as Homans Associates LLC (“Homans”), a Watsco subsidiary, in the Northeast U.S. Subsequently, Carrier Enterprise II purchased Carrier’s distribution operations in Mexico.

In 2009, we formed a joint venture with Carrier , which we refer to as Carrier Enterprise I, in which Carrier contributed company-owned locations in various Sun Belt states and Puerto Rico, and its export division in Miami, Florida, and we contributed certain locations that distributed Carrier products.
In 2019, we repurchased the 20% ownership interest in Homans from Carrier Enterprise II and have since solely owned and operated Homans.
In 2012, we formed a third joint venture with Carrier, which we refer to as Carrier Enterprise III, to which Carrier contributed company-owned locations in Canada.
